The campaign focuses on telecommunications networks, which provide access to large volumes of sensitive communications data and can serve as strategic intelligence collection points for nation-state actors.

The second tool, PeerTime, is an ELF-based backdoor designed to run across multiple processor architectures, including ARM, MIPS, PowerPC and AArch64, enabling it to infect a range of Linux servers, routers and embedded systems commonly deployed in telecommunications environments.
The intrusions add to a growing body of reported Chinese espionage activity against telecommunications providers globally.

The exact initial access method used in the attacks is not known, although the adversary has previously targeted systems running outdated versions of Windows Server and Microsoft Exchange Server to drop web shells for follow-on activity.
